title: Development and Validation of Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy Risk Scores for Every Level of Care: A Multicentric, International Study
summary:
The TRACE-AMY study aims to develop and test simple, reliable risk scores to help identify people with transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy, a condition in which an abnormal protein builds up in the heart and makes it harder to work properly.

The components of risk scores will be considered based on the warning signs of the disease and underlying biological processes that cause the disease and will  be designed for use in different healthcare settings, from general practice to specialist centres. Unlike existing tools, the new scores will not use general demographic predictors like age or sex to estimate risk. Instead, they will focus on factors directly related to the disease and be developed in and for the group of patients with thickening of the heart’s main pumping chamber (left ventricular hypertrophy), in whom considering the diagnosis of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy is particularly important. This approach aims to help detect transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy earlier, when treatment may be most beneficial, and reduce the risk of the condition being missed in women.
The study will be carried out at multiple centres across different countries.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- enddiastolic left ventricular wall thickness ≥ 12mm
- guideline-concordant diagnosis of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy or exclusion of cardiac amyloidosis
Exclusion criteria:
- lack of multimodal characterization, including clinical and laboratory assessment, ECG and comprehensive transthoracic echocardiography
